text:
Maya: quick thread - thinking about the rollout UX for a new route-aware sampling policy. This one changes head vs tail thresholds per customer tier and adds route-level retention budgets. need opinions on safe canary + console signals we should show.
Ken: big +1. we should have a simulation endpoint in the console so owners can preview projected span retention and cost delta before applying.
Olivia: fyi some exporters (OTLP gRPC) will start dropping when we flip aggressive tail sampling at SDK level, so we need a graceful throttle not a hard switch.
Raj: agree on gradual. proposal: 5% canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if error_rate or retention misses target by X. rollbacks should be per-tenant.
Maya: exact signals? thinking: retained_span_count, sampling_rate_estimate, exporter_queue_drops, and CPU/gRPC latency. also show projected monthly token/spans saved in console.
Ken: add a small simulator that accepts a sample of recent traces and applies the policy to estimate visibility loss. endpoint: POST /api/v1/simulate-sampler {route, policy, window_minutes} -> returns numbers + example dropped-span ids.
Olivia: implementation note: SDKs need a "soft mode" where they mark spans as "candidate-drop" and the collector can still accept them but tag for lower retention class. that avoids sudden exporter OOMs.
Raj: we should expose a console toggle for "apply in soft mode" vs "hard enforce". default to soft for first 72h.
Devex-Lia: from UX side: owners want a single view: a timeline with canary % steps, key risk signals (exporter drops, increased tail latency), and an estimated cost curve. also quick revert button that creates a rollback change and an audit entry.
Maya: what about telemetry retention budgeting? owners may want to spend X spans/month for a route. console should show consumption vs budget and warn when applying policy would exceed reserved budget.
Ken: +1 - expose per-route budget alerts and an automatic throttle when budget is close. throttle should operate on request routing upstream so we don't create noisy collector load.
Olivia: related: need to document how this interacts with exporter batching and OTLP backoff. quick snippet for SDK behavior we discussed:
```json
{
  "policy": "route-aware",
  "mode": "soft",
  "head_sampling": 1.0,
  "tail_sampling": 0.1,
  "budget": 100000
}
```
Raj: tiny ops detail - canary metadata must include the exact policy json and a random seed so sampling is deterministic across services during canary. avoids split-brain sampling.
Devex-Lia: UI copy: show "Predicted visibility loss: 3% - 8%" and a help tooltip linking to a simulated examples page. also include a cost-savings estimate.
sampling-bot: deploy event: canary 5% for policy 1765436789 applied to routes [payments:v2, search:v1] by Maya.
Maya: deployed the 5% canary. starting 2h warmup window. monitoring dashboards updated: sampler.canary.* metrics + exporter.queue_drops.
Ken: I'll wire the simulation API to the console this morning. quick ask: what retention horizon do we sample against for estimation? last 24h or 7d?
Olivia: 24h should be default for quick feedback, 7d for accurate cost estimate. compute cost scales, cache results if same window+policy.
Raj: can we have an automatic test that runs the simulation on every sampling config PR and logs expected signal deltas? helps catch egregious visibility loss.
Maya: yes - add to CI: simulate on a 1h sample and fail if visibility loss > 25% for any critical route.
Devex-Lia: note for console: make canary steps editable (owner may prefer 10/30/60) and surface a "recommended" path with green checks.
Ken: sounds good. I'll open a draft PR for the sim endpoint + console mockups.
Olivia: ping me on the SDK changes - I'll add the soft-mode tag and collector-side policy to accept candidate drops for 72h.
Maya: thanks all - sync tomorrow 11am to review PR and dashboard widgets. :thumbsup:
